jenna: Customer (acme-med) seeing intermittent streaming cutoff ~60s, then 502 on reconnect. Happened across 3 pods in us-west-2 around 2026-03-16T03:12:xxZ. Sample request id: rq_3a1f2c9b. They sit behind a corporate proxy and use signed-cookie auth. Need a minimal curl that reproduces the streaming handshake + auth and a short checklist of what logs/captures to collect for a debug bundle.

ryan: Can you paste the exact failing request-id(s) and the route/model they hit? Also whether the customer uses SSE or chunked HTTP streaming (server-sent events vs newline-delimited tokens).

jenna: Request ids: rq_3a1f2c9b, rq_7b2e9d4f, rq_9c8a1b00. They hit /v1/streams (model=redwood-text-stream) with Accept: text/event-stream (SSE).

mike: Minimal verified curl I use for reproducing SSE + auth behind a proxy. Replace envs and run from a machine that mimics their network:

```bash
# set these first
export TOKEN='REPLACE_WITH_BEARER'
export COOKIE='__Secure-signed=REPLACE; Path=/; HttpOnly'
export PROXY='http://corp-proxy.local:3128'  # if customer uses one

curl --no-buffer --http2 -v \
  --proxy "$PROXY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: rq_3a1f2c9b" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "User-Agent: acme-repro/1.0" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  --cookie "$COOKIE" \
  --include \
  "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-text-stream&temperature=0.2"
```

Notes:--no-buffer keeps stdout unbuffered so SSE events show up live, --http2 matches our frontdoor when enabled, --include (-i) shows response headers, -v gives TLS handshake debug. If the stream cuts, save the full curl -v output (redirect both stdout/stderr).

ivan: If they use a proxy that rewrites connection headers or terminates TLS, encourage them to run the same curl from a machine outside the proxy (home laptop) to compare. Also collect a short tcpdump around the failure window:

```bash
# run for ~2 minutes and stop after repro
sudo timeout 120 tcpdump -i any host api.redwoodinference.com and port 443 -w /tmp/stream-rq_3a1f2c9b.pcap
```

And collect the raw curl logs:

```bash
curl --no-buffer --http2 -v --include ...  https://... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/curl-rq_3a1f2c9b.log
```

mike: From our side we need: server-side proxy logs (if any), the backend pod logs around the request ids (search for rq_3a1f2c9b), any TLS reneg negotiation entries, and the frontdoor LB logs showing connection durations. If they can share the pcap and curl log (redact tokens) we can correlate.

support-bot: Checklist for debug bundle :white_check_mark:
• curl -v output (redirect stderr->file and include)
• tcpdump/pcap for the timeframe
• application logs with request ids (timestamps)
• proxy access logs (if corporate proxy used)
• exact curl command used and environment (OS, curl version)
• note whether issue reproduces from another network

jenna: I'll send the curl + tcpdump instructions to the customer and ask them to redact tokens and include the three request ids. Any tweaks you recommend to the command above?

mike: small tweak — if they see truncated SSE frames, ask them to add `--raw` to avoid libcurl decoding; also try removing `--http2` if their proxy/old middlebox mishandles HTTP/2. Quick example toggle: `--http2` vs `--http1.1`.

ivan: Also try adding `-H \"X-Debug-Force-Trace: true\"` if they can pass a debug header to surface extra tracing on our side (only if you have customer consent).

ryan: Once they send pcap + curl log, I'll pull LB traces and correlate by X-Request-Id and timestamps. Thanks — keep me looped.

jenna: Thanks all — sending now. I'll attach their responses here when I have them. :thumbsup:
